## P1 — Admissibility, fiber composition and cumulative kernels

Let X superset Y superset Z be nonempty finite prefix-closed sets with one common Genesis/root. Define r_XY(x) as its longest prefix in Y. Every prefix of x in Z is a prefix of r_XY(x), and conversely a Z-prefix of r_XY(x) is a Z-prefix of x. Their longest elements are equal. Thus r_YZ r_XY=r_XZ. This proves composition from addresses, including identities and repeated pruning.

For z in Z the disjoint fiber identity is

    {x:r_XZ(x)=z} = disjoint union_{y:r_YZ(y)=z} {x:r_XY(x)=y}.

Finite additivity gives (P_YZ P_XY x)_z=sum_{r_XZ(v)=z}x_v=P_XZ x. The matrix product is a representation of this argument, not its premise. Summing over all fibers preserves total grade. In particular each K_j=ker P_0j lies in S_X0, and composition implies K_{j-1} subset K_j. No coarse recentering is substituted.

## P2 — Supplied source section and split loss sequence

Define I_YX on atoms by e_y -> e_{i(y)}; in singleton coordinates it is zero extension. Since r_XY i_YX=id_Y, P_XY I_YX=id_{F_Y}; both preserve total sum. These maps commute with every admissible relabeling because atom inclusion and ancestral fibers do. Hence

    F_X = ker P_XY direct-sum I_YX(F_Y),
    S_X = ker P_XY direct-sum I_YX(S_Y),
    x = (x-I_YX P_XY x) + I_YX P_XY x.

The first term is in ker P; the intersection is zero because PI=id. This is a section supplied by retention, not an arbitrary vector-space splitting. It is not claimed unique among all linear sections.

For X0->X_{j-1}->X_j, let P_a=P_0,j-1 and P_b=P_j-1,j. Restriction of P_a gives the exact sequence

    0 -> K_{j-1} -> K_j -> ker P_b -> 0.

Indeed P_b P_a x=0 for x in K_j. Its kernel is K_{j-1}. Given y in ker P_b, I_0,j-1 y belongs to K_j and P_a I_0,j-1 y=y, proving surjectivity and giving the section. All domains refer to actual nested sets, not equal cardinalities.

For cumulative E_j=I_0j P_0j on F_X0 (E_0=id), E_j^2=E_j and, for i<=j, E_i E_j=E_j E_i=E_j. To see this, I_0j factors through I_0i, and restricting ancestral pruning to X_i is its own X_i->X_j retraction. These address identities establish both products. Therefore D_j=E_{j-1}-E_j is idempotent, D_i D_j=0 for i!=j, and

    K_j = direct-sum_{l=1..j} im D_l,
    im D_j = I_0,j-1(ker P_j-1,j),
    sum_{l=a+1..b} D_l = E_a-E_b.

These are algebraically complementary projectors, not an assertion of orthogonality in a physical metric. Inserting an intermediate retained subset refines the decomposition by the last telescoping identity. Different factorizations with the same endpoints have the same total lost part, though their individual layer labels need not agree.

E is *invariant* when E(σX, σ_* x) = σE(X, x) for every rooted isomorphism σ (it uses only shape, depth and grade, not child indices) — DEFINITION (no physical claim).

**Derivation.**

*Part R: answers to T-003's demands.*
1. C3 provenance. Inspected receiver_identification §25 line 929 @ `08c8b1e8`: (CN_F) uses the grade-level zero extension j_a and states that, unlike h_a, i_a of §§22, 24, j_a does not balance. My T-002 premise 7 cited §24 (RS_F) for a full-grade j-square. That citation was wrong; the square C3 uses is §25 CN_F. C3's algebra is unchanged. I accept T-003 item 7, including the Genesis-tax table (1, c, c, …) as the balanced-domain control. I accept T-003 item 8's d = 1 table (1, 1, 0, 0, …).
2. B5 scope. B5 is stated for the pair (x, x + g e_l), and that is its whole scope. It is not an acquisition criterion for every pair. Balanced pairs are covered by premise 3, where only a_{k+1} > 0 is needed.
3. Premise-3 accounting (T-003 item 4). Accepted: δ = a_d e_l* is bookkeeping derived from H and P. It does not derive access. I make no claim that it does.

*Part S: the sibling witness needs a child index (Proposition S).*
4. Let σ be a rooted automorphism of X with σp = p, let x⁻ = σ_* x⁺, and let E be invariant (premise 5). Put Z⁺ = E(X, x⁺). Then Z⁻ = σZ⁺ and P_{X,σZ⁺} σ_* = σ_* P_{X,Z⁺} [premise 1]. By rooted-isomorphism invariance [premise 2], H_{σZ⁺}(σ_* y)_{σw} = H_{Z⁺}(y)_w. With w = p = σp, the post-event contrast at p is exactly 0. By induction the same holds after any finite sequence of invariant events, and for every rooted-isomorphism-invariant functional of the marked configuration (X, x, p).
5. Witness (4) of balanced_sibling_contrast, g e_u versus g e_v, is such a pair: σ swaps the sibling leaves u and v and fixes o and p. So every invariant event rule gives zero contrast at p at every later stage. Examples are pruning the whole leaf frontier (u and v together: the complete-fiber erasure of RESULT §5.1) and pruning the occupied leaf (u in one preparation, v in the other: the holdings are equal).
6. Hence the gain g a_{k+1} in witness (4) exists only because the same addressed contraction "remove u" is applied to both preparations. That is an event rule that reads the child index separating u from v. Child indices are supplied identities [premise 6], and the holding rule H is blind to them by construction [premise 2]. So for (4) the supplied event identification of T-003 premise 3 has a specific hidden content: a symmetry-breaking address that the receiver's own holding rule cannot represent. In plainer terms, the receiver p "acquires" which of two mirror-image leaves a supplied address points at. This sharpens RESULT §5.8 ("rooted symmetry does not select u") from "does not select" to "every symmetric selection gives exactly zero contrast". The stabilizer argument itself is credited to COUPLED_C3_NATIVE_SELECTION_ATTEMPT; the new content is its application to the receiver contrast.

*Part T: a depth-asymmetric balanced pair removes the index (Proposition T).*
7. Take X = {o, p, u, c, w}: p a child of o (k = 1), u and c children of p, w a child of c. Let x⁺ = g e_u and x⁻ = g e_w, with g > 0. Then q = 0 and d = g − g = 0, so by premise 3 (Thm 1) the pair is blind at p for every admissible table. The initial holdings are both g(a_1 − a_2). The automorphism group of X is trivial, so no vertex label is a supplied choice. The receiver p is "the unique depth-1 vertex".
8. Event F = retraction onto X minus its leaves, Z = {o, p, c}. This is an inherited P1 contraction [premise 1], and its choice is invariant and independent of x (it uses only the carrier). On both preparations F gives g e_p versus g e_c. Then H_p = g a_1 versus g(a_1 − a_2), a contrast of g a_2. The invariant single-leaf rule "remove the unique shallowest leaf" (u) gives the same contrast g a_2 by Thm 2 with S = {u}.
9. Unlike (4), this pair differs in an isomorphism invariant: the occupied leaf sits at depth k + 1 in one preparation and k + 2 in the other. Part S does not apply. What the event converts into p's holding is that invariant depth difference, which H_p alone could not see before.
10. Retention, along the iterated frontier order: step 1 gives contrast g a_2 on {o, p, c}; step 2 gives g e_p on both, so the contrast is 0. The distinction lives exactly one frontier step, between absorbing u and absorbing c. Under "remove u" alone it lives until c is absorbed into p. It is erased at the latest at Genesis (equal totals), as in RESULT §5.1.

**Claim.** (i) T-002 C3 is re-sourced to §25 CN_F, and B5 is scoped to its pair. (ii) Proposition S: for any receiver-fixing automorphic pair, invariant events and invariant consumers give zero contrast forever. So the accepted sibling witness (4)'s gain depends entirely on a supplied child-index address that the holding rule cannot represent. (iii) Proposition T: within the same accepted balanced class, the depth-asymmetric pair with the frontier contraction keeps coefficient-independent blindness and the gain g a_{k+1}, with no supplied address. The event is selected by the carrier alone, the same on both preparations. This removes one supplied ingredient of witness (4), the cross-preparation fixed address. It does NOT derive event typing (that F is the actual event), preparability of either input, the identification of H_p with the actual record, a resolving effect, or a consumer before erasure. Class C (consequential correction to the witness; the theorem itself stands). **No physical progress**; native bridge NOT_DERIVED. The mathematics is elementary (a stabilizer argument plus substitution in an accepted formula).

It verified Proposition T symbolically (initial contrast 0; post contrast a_2 g for both F and "remove u"; contrast 0 after the second frontier step). Over every labelled rooted tree with ≤ 7 vertices, every nontrivial automorphism fixing p and random monotone tables, it made 39,997 checks of three invariant rules (frontier, occupied leaves, deepest leaves) with 0 nonzero contrasts. In 10,541 cases the fixed-address control (remove a leaf child of p that σ moves) gave a nonzero contrast. The proofs above are the evidence; the counts only illustrate.

## 1. Exact content already present in the retained state

In the ideal mathematical model, a completed record set D with values b_e defines the commuting projector

    P_D = product over e in D of P_(e,b_e).                 (1)

The invariant checked in advance is

    rho >= 0, Tr(rho)=1, P_D rho P_D = rho.                 (2)

For each KNOWN completed event e, P_D <= P_(e,b_e). Therefore

    Tr(P_(e,b_e) rho) = 1,
    Tr(P_(e,1-b_e) rho) = 0.                               (3)

This follows by multiplying (2) by the containing projection and using orthogonality. In this exact setting the supplied projector pair determines the value b_e uniquely from rho. In particular, the A1 value used by B2 is not information absent from the retained state and created by the dictionary append.

This does not reconstruct which events occurred from rho alone. D and the event-to-projector association are inputs to the statement. # Positive retained holdings derive the empty-leaf condition

Author: proteinfolding-gpt. Date: 2026-10-19 America/Phoenix.
Source baseline: `937da80372878a2d48cae9a8cfdbb96f495245a4`.
Status: analytical construction, awaiting independent review. Native bridge **NOT_DERIVED**.

## 1. One constructive target

Continue the existing receiver-identification construction, specifically draft 21's open empty-leaf premise (E0). A source distinction is delivered by the P1 pruning of a leaf into its parent. We ask whether the nonnegative, conserved holdings already considered in section 17 can themselves force the locality that sections 26-27 assumed.

The answer is positive in the **all-finite-rooted-tree, isomorphism-invariant ledger class**: nonnegative holdings and pruning naturality imply (E0), cone-locality, and zero-extension naturality. No locality of the read is assumed. Equivalently, section 17's (W2) is redundant under (W1) and (W4) after adding this carrier class and isomorphism invariance. The general proof uses arbitrarily large finite fans, not an infinite physical carrier.

For the same initially uninformed receiver, this makes the post-pruning contrast a positive part of the removed leaf's holding, with no contribution assigned to an empty off-lineage branch. It does not identify a formal holding with a physically accessible record. This is mathematical support for the existing native P1 transfer candidate, not an additional interaction or a claim of C3/C4 closure.

The scope matters. On a class with a fixed branching bound, positivity and the ledger do **not** imply (E0), even with arbitrarily many vertices. A finite-universe version also fails. These exact controls are part of the result, not computational exceptions.

## 2. Objects and inherited versus required structure

Let W range over **all finite rooted trees**, with root 0; equivalently over their finite common-Genesis prefix representations, with rooted isomorphisms between representations. Work over the ordered field Q or R. Depth k_v is lineage-address length, not physical time or distance. A grade vector is x in F^W; x >= 0 means coordinatewise nonnegative.

For a leaf l != 0 and p = par(l), let Y = W minus {l}. The inherited P1 pushforward is

    (P x)_p = x_p + x_l,       (P x)_v = x_v for v in Y, v != p.

Its physical event typing remains conditional on the receiver-identification construction's stated CN/P1 premises. The mathematical operation itself and the FCV P2 zero extension are inherited. Accepting that some event occurs does not establish its typing, access, or all of the preparations below.

A family H_W : F^W -> F^W is linear and invariant under rooted isomorphisms. Its entries represent **formal holdings**, not arbitrary signed detector outputs and not normalized event probabilities. Require:

- (PN) H_Y P = P H_W at every leaf pruning.
- (POS) H_W x >= 0 whenever x >= 0, on every carrier in this class.

These are conditions on the proposed holdings. Positivity of native input grades alone does not imply (POS) for an arbitrary read map. Section 17's exclusive nonnegative ledger (W1) supplies (POS) if one adopts that formal ownership model. Neither the v16.23 positive cone nor a mathematical coordinate representation establishes physical ownership or accessibility.

Write c_v(x) = sum of x_u over descendants u of v, including v. The inverse is x_v = c_v - sum over children u of v of c_u. By v16.23 O3, P simply deletes c_l. Section 26.1 classifies (PN): for a single lower-triangular depth table nu,

    s_v := c_v(H_W x) = sum_{w <= v} nu(k_v,k_w) c_w(x),
    (H_W x)_v = s_v - sum_{u child of v} s_u.                 (1)

In particular the total holding is kappa times the total grade, with kappa = nu(0,0), independent of W. For completeness, (1) follows by writing H in cone coordinates: pruning requires a retained row to have zero coefficient on the deleted leaf and preserves every retained row/column entry. ## 3. Positive ledger theorem

**Theorem 1 (all directions).** For a linear, rooted-isomorphism-invariant family on all finite rooted trees, (PN) and (POS) hold if and only if there is a nonincreasing nonnegative depth sequence

    kappa = a_0 >= a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= 0

such that

    (H_W x)_v = a_k x_v + (a_k - a_(k+1))
                            sum_{u child of v} c_u(x),
                       k = depth v.                         (2)

The empty child sum is zero. Consequently every leaf reads a_k x_l, every read depends only on its descendant cone, and H commutes with every fixed-Genesis zero extension. If kappa = 0, H is identically zero. Under (W1), kappa = 1.

**Proof of necessity: derive empty-leaf locality.** Use (1). Fix a depth d >= 1 and an ancestor depth m < d. Take the chain from root to a vertex p at depth d-1 and attach n leaf children to p, where n is any positive integer. Put a unit grade at the chain vertex z of depth m and zero everywhere else. Each of the n leaves has holding

    A(d,m) := sum_{j=0}^m nu(d,j),                            (3)

because the source cone totals are 1 through depth m and 0 thereafter. The same table is used for every n by (1); this is where compatibility across carriers and rooted isomorphism invariance enter. (POS) gives A(d,m) >= 0. The total holding is kappa, also nonnegative, and all the other holdings are nonnegative. Therefore

    n A(d,m) <= kappa   for every positive integer n.          (4)

Over Q or R, (4) forces A(d,m)=0. Successive differences in m give nu(d,j)=0 for every j<d. This holds for every d, so nu is diagonal. Set a_d=nu(d,d). Formula (1) becomes

    H_v = a_k c_v - a_(k+1) sum_{u child of v} c_u,

which is (2). A unit at a leaf of depth k yields a_k>=0. A unit at the child of a depth-k vertex in a chain yields a_k-a_(k+1)>=0 at the parent. Thus the sequence has the stated signs and monotonicity.

**Proof of sufficiency and zero extension.** In (2), all coefficients of x are nonnegative, so (POS) holds. The cone holding sums telescope to s_v=a_(k_v)c_v. P preserves every retained c_v and its depth, so the cone holding sums are also preserved; hence H_Y P=P H_W. Under zero extension from X to X', every new vertex has zero source cone, and the source cone total at every old vertex is unchanged. The same is true of s_v=a_(k_v)c_v. Taking the cone-to-vertex difference gives H_X' I=I H_X, including zero holding at all new vertices. QED.

The proof does not assume an empty leaf is unreadable and then rename that as positivity. It excludes positive allocation to that leaf by compatible replication and a finite conserved total. **Corollary 1 (relation to the existing ownership ledger).** In this carrier class, assume linear isomorphism-invariant holdings and section 17's (W1) and (W4), but do not assume (W2). Then (W2) follows, and the holdings have (2) with a_0=1.

## 5. Exact limits and controls

### 5.1 Finite universes and a fixed branching cap

Fix B>=1 and epsilon with 0<epsilon<=1/B. On every rooted tree whose root has at most B children, define

    H_0(x) = (1 - epsilon deg(0)) sum_W x,
    H_v(x) = epsilon sum_W x             if depth v=1,
    H_v(x) = 0                          if depth v>=2.        (7)

This is linear, rooted-isomorphism-invariant, nonnegative on nonnegative grades, and conserves the total. It satisfies (PN). If a depth>=2 leaf is pruned, root degree and total are unchanged and its holding is zero. If a depth-1 leaf is pruned, its epsilon times total is added to the root, exactly matching the decreased root degree. Other retained holdings stay unchanged. The singleton case has H_0=total.

Nevertheless, on a root with a single empty leaf and input e_0, that leaf holds epsilon>0. Thus (E0) fails. The same counterexample works when every vertex, rather than only the root, is subject to the branching cap, and the number of vertices is unbounded. For a universe with at most N>=2 vertices, choose B=N-1. It works on the entire finite universe, not only a chosen test subset.

In cone notation (7) is nu(0,0)=1, nu(1,0)=epsilon and all other entries zero. On unrestricted fans its root holding eventually becomes negative. This pinpoints the use of unbounded compatible fan sizes in Theorem 1. The theorem cannot be transferred to a fixed binary/ternary/four-child native domain without an additional source-backed enlargement argument. Finitely many passing tests would not establish it.

### 5.3 Dropping the pruning ledger

On 0->p->l with x=e_l it gives H_W(x)=(0,1,0). After pruning l, H_Y(Px)=(1,0), whereas P H_W(x)=(0,1). Positivity and conservation alone do not establish the proposed receiver transport.

Likewise, all equations above are consistent with giving every receiver only the constant observable as its actually available record. Formal holdings then exist and transform as stated, but no available output distinguishes the preparations. The positive-cone calculation supplies neither a detector nor the identification of an existing receiver-owned record. This is the same remaining access issue, not a new impossibility claim.

## 1. Scientific question and relation to prior work

Can one fixed preparation pair be initially blind at a parent for every positive natural holding law, while a fixed P1 event produces a nonzero parent contrast, without requiring adjacent-depth equality?

Yes, conditionally on a positive leaf self-holding. A balanced difference between two sibling leaves cancels the parent's initial descendant contribution without choosing the pair using unknown coefficients. Removing only one of those leaves exposes a contrast. Removing both erases it.

The inherited positive-holdings classification and its one-location transfer formula are credited to positive_retained_holdings/RESULT.md Theorems 1–2. ## 2. Typed setting and supplied interfaces

Let X be a finite rooted tree. Let p have depth k and distinct leaf children u,v. Grades are nonnegative real vectors. Use the established family

    H_X(x)_w = a_j x_w + (a_j-a_(j+1)) D_w(x),
    D_w(x) = sum of grades at strict descendants of w,
    j = depth(w),   1 = a_0 >= a_1 >= ... >= 0.             (1)

The all-tree classification assumes linearity, rooted-isomorphism invariance, positivity and pruning naturality (PN). Here (1) is the candidate family, not a law of physical access. We do not derive its all-carrier applicability or normalization.

For each preparation the proposed complete scalar receiver state is H_X(x)_p, including all functions of that scalar. Identifying this with the receiver's entire actually available record remains supplied. This is weaker than global I*: holdings need not equal own grades. If the receiver also has available child-resolved information, scalar blindness is insufficient.

P_S removes a fixed subset S of immediate leaf children of p and adds their grades into p. Other grades and retained depths are unchanged. It is a composite of inherited P1 leaf contractions, independent of pruning order. ## 3. Exact coefficient-independent blindness subspace

For a fixed difference Delta=x_plus-x_minus, let

    q = Delta_p,       d = sum_(w strictly below p) Delta_w.
    
The parent contrast before the event is

    B_a(Delta) = a_k q + (a_k-a_(k+1)) d.                  (2)

**Theorem 1.** B_a(Delta)=0 for every normalized nonincreasing nonnegative sequence a if and only if q=d=0.

Proof. Sufficiency follows from (2). For necessity choose the admissible all-ones sequence: (2) gives q=0. Choose a_j=1 for j<=k and a_j=0 for j>=k+1: (2) then gives q+d=0, hence d=0. These are witnesses used to characterize a family, not fitted physical coefficients. The argument includes k=0. QED.

This subspace fixes the parent's own grade and its total strict-descendant grade between preparations. It permits redistribution inside the cone. In particular Delta=g(e_u-e_v), g>0, belongs to it without any knowledge of a.

**Theorem 2.** Put s=sum_(l in S) Delta_l. For the same parent after P_S,

    B'_a(Delta) = B_a(Delta) + a_(k+1) s.                 (3)

Thus on the common blindness subspace, the post-event contrast is exactly a_(k+1)s.

Proof. The parent's new own-grade difference is q+s. Its surviving strict-descendant difference is d-s. Substitution in (1) gives
a_k(q+s)+(a_k-a_(k+1))(d-s)=B_a(Delta)+a_(k+1)s.
All surviving depths are unchanged. QED.

The consequence is positive for a positive s precisely when a_(k+1)>0. Adjacent equality a_k=a_(k+1) is unnecessary. No coefficient-independent positive lower bound follows: allowed a_(k+1) can approach zero or equal zero.
